verdict.rationale: Muse's own docs say that once a goal or task is set, it keeps working on a schedule and in response to events after the app is closed. It follows up and sends a notification when something needs attention, which covers automatic background runs that report back. However, nothing documents user-defined scheduling, such as choosing a recurring cadence or a specific one-off run time, versus Muse deciding its own schedule. Missing for 10: explicit user-configurable recurring schedules, explicit one-off timed tasks, documentation of how results are delivered beyond notifications, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can schedule recurring or one-off tasks that run automatically and come back to me with results

citations.quote: Once you've set a goal or a task, Muse continues to work on a schedule and in response to relevant events, taking the next step and following up
Muse keeps things moving after you close the app. It monitors, follows up, and sends a notification when something needs your attention, so nothing falls through the cracks.
The Goals tab is where Muse keeps track of all this for you, and you can interact directly there or talk to it about these tasks in chat.
